b: The eye level is the height of the viewer’s eye above the ground, usually represented by a horizontal line running across the picture, even if the horizon itself is not visible in the scene.
So yes. Eye level and horizon are essentially synonymous. They’re one and the same thing in the preliminary line drawing of the dinosaur on the beach, where the ocean is in view.
It's a little above the heads of the running kids, (nieces and nephews at a big family gathering).

In most scenes, you can't see all the way to the horizon line. Either you’re in a forest, or you’re inside a room or the view is hemmed in with buildings.
The eye level is one of the first lines you put into your drawing, even a figure drawing at a sketch group. I mark it with the letters EL to remind me what it is.
Everything that you draw above the line is something you’re looking up at. In a view that’s more of a downshot, the EL is high in the composition because almost everything in the scene is below your level gaze.
